add-136.title: Japanese Cotton Cheesecake
add-136.culturalNotes: The whites must reach soft, not stiff, peaks or the cake will crack. The water bath and low heat are the secret of its wobbly, cotton-like texture.

add-136-i9.name: Cream of tartar or lemon juice

instructions.1: Melt the cream cheese, butter and milk over a water bath, stirring until smooth, and let cool slightly.
instructions.2: Add the yolks one at a time, then the vanilla, then sift in the flour and cornflour and whisk until smooth.
instructions.3: Whisk the whites with the cream of tartar until foamy, then add the sugar gradually until soft, curling peaks form (not stiff).
instructions.4: Fold the whites into the cheese mixture in three additions, pour into a lined tin and tap out the bubbles.
instructions.5: Set the tin in a tray of warm water 2 cm deep and bake at 150°C for 60-70 minutes until risen and golden.
instructions.6: Turn off the oven and leave the door ajar 15-20 minutes before taking it out so it doesn't sink, then cool.

add-137.title: Red Grape Jam
add-137.culturalNotes: Citric acid preserves the jam and stops it crystallising. Red grapes give a beautiful colour with no need for colouring.

add-137-i4.name: Citric acid (or juice of 1 large lemon)

instructions.1: Pick the grapes off the bunches, wash well and discard any shrivelled ones.
instructions.2: Put the grapes, sugar, water and citric acid in a heavy-based pot and stir gently.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil over medium heat, then simmer about 40 minutes until the grapes are cooked and the syrup thickens, skimming the foam.
instructions.4: Test with a spoonful on a cold plate; if it holds its shape it is done.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-138.title: Jordanian Shrak Bread
add-138.culturalNotes: Shrak is the bedouin bread of Jordan and Palestine and is served under the rice in mansaf. The simple yeast-free dough and a very hot saj are the secret of its thinness.

add-138-i1.name: White flour (or 2 cups white + 1 cup wholemeal)

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and sugar, add the water gradually and knead 8-10 minutes into a smooth, supple dough that doesn't stick.
instructions.2: Divide into orange-sized balls, brush with oil, cover and rest an hour until relaxed.
instructions.3: Roll each ball with a rolling pin, then stretch it over the backs of your hands, tossing between them until very thin and translucent.
instructions.4: Heat the domed saj (or the back of a large upturned wok) well, drape the loaf over it and leave a few seconds until bubbles appear, then flip for a few seconds more.
instructions.5: Fold the loaves and stack them under a cloth so they stay soft.

add-139.title: Fresh Peach Juice
add-139.culturalNotes: Lemon stops the juice browning and brings out the peach flavour. Very ripe peaches need little sugar.

instructions.1: Peel the peaches (easy after 30 seconds in boiling water then iced water) and cut them up.
instructions.2: Blend with the water, sugar and lemon until completely smooth.
instructions.3: Strain for a light juice, or leave it thick.
instructions.4: Serve chilled with mint leaves.

add-140.title: Arayes (Meat-Stuffed Grilled Pita)
add-140.culturalNotes: The meat layer must be thin so it cooks at the same time as the bread crisps, and draining the onion and tomato stops the bread going soggy.

add-140-i1.name: Minced meat with a little fat

add-140-i3.name: Onion, very finely chopped and drained

add-140-i8.name: Olive oil with paprika for brushing the bread

instructions.1: Knead the meat with the onion, tomato, parsley, pomegranate molasses and spices until even.
instructions.2: Open each loaf at one edge like a pocket and spread a thin, even layer of meat inside right to the edges, pressing it flat.
instructions.3: Brush the outside of the bread with the paprika olive oil and cut each loaf into quarters or halves.
instructions.4: Arrange in a tray and bake at 200°C for 10 minutes, then flip and bake 8-10 minutes until crisp and the meat is cooked.
instructions.5: They can also be grilled over charcoal or in an electric grill until crisp on both sides.
instructions.6: Serve hot with tahini and pickles.

add-141.title: Kazandibi (Turkish Caramelized Milk Pudding)
add-141.culturalNotes: Kazandibi means 'bottom of the pot' in Turkish, as the base is deliberately scorched. Mastic is the authentic Ottoman flavour.

add-141-i7.name: Mastic ground with a little sugar

instructions.1: Grease a rectangular metal tray with the butter and sprinkle the sugar evenly over the base.
instructions.2: Whisk the milk, sugar, rice flour and flour cold, then stir constantly over medium heat until thick and boiling for 2 minutes; add the mastic and vanilla.
instructions.3: Set the empty tray directly on the heat until the sugar caramelises and turns brown, then pour the pudding over it at once.
instructions.4: Move the tray over the heat so the whole base browns evenly (1-2 minutes) without burning.
instructions.5: Let cool, then chill 4 hours, cut into rectangles and roll each piece so the caramelised side faces up.

add-142.title: Turkish Trileçe (Three-Milk Caramel Cake)
add-142.culturalNotes: Trileçe is the Balkan-Turkish version of Latin American tres leches cake, set apart by its glossy caramel topping.

add-142-i4.name: Baking powder and a pinch of salt

add-142-i11.name: For the caramel: butter and warm cream

instructions.1: Whisk the whites until firm and the yolks with the sugar and vanilla until pale, fold in the whites gently, then sift in the flour and baking powder and fold lightly.
instructions.2: Pour into a greased tray and bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden; let it cool to warm.
instructions.3: Mix the milk, cream and condensed milk, prick the warm cake with a fork and pour the mixture over gradually until absorbed; chill overnight.
instructions.4: For the caramel: melt the sugar in a pan until amber, then carefully add the butter and warm cream, stirring until smooth, and let cool.
instructions.5: Spread the whipped cream over the cake, pour the caramel sauce on top and cut into cold squares.

add-143.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
add-143.culturalNotes: Brown sugar gives the cookies softness and a caramel flavour, and taking them out while the centre is soft makes them chewy inside and crisp at the edges.

instructions.1: Cream the butter with both sugars until light and pale, then add the eggs and vanilla.
instructions.2: Add the flour, soda and salt and mix just until no flour shows, then fold in the chocolate chips.
instructions.3: Chill the dough 30 minutes, then scoop tablespoon-sized balls onto a lined tray, spaced apart.
instructions.4: Bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until the edges colour and the centres are still soft.
instructions.5: Leave on the tray 5 minutes to firm up, then move to a rack to cool.

add-144.title: Muhammara (Red Pepper and Walnut Dip)
add-144.culturalNotes: Muhammara is an Aleppo mezze, and pomegranate molasses gives it a balanced sweet-sour taste. Its flavour improves if left an hour before serving.

instructions.1: Roast the peppers over a direct flame or under the grill until blackened, cover 10 minutes, then peel and seed.
instructions.2: Lightly toast the walnuts in a dry pan.
instructions.3: Chop the walnuts coarsely in a processor, then add the peppers, garlic, pepper paste, pomegranate molasses, spices and lemon and process.
instructions.4: Add the breadcrumbs and olive oil and process until creamy with some texture.
instructions.5: Serve in a dish drizzled with olive oil and walnuts, or spread on manakish dough before baking.

add-145.title: Za'atar Manakish
add-145.culturalNotes: Manakish is the most famous morning breakfast in Lebanon and the Levant. The fingertip dimples hold the za'atar oil so it doesn't run off the dough.

instructions.1: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and oil with the warm water into a smooth dough, cover an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Mix the za'atar with the olive oil into a runny paste.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into 8 balls, roll each into a thin round and press with your fingertips to make small dimples.
instructions.4: Spread the za'atar mixture over the top, leaving a small border.
instructions.5: Bake on a saj or tray in an oven preheated to the highest heat for 7-10 minutes until the edges brown.
instructions.6: Serve hot with tomato, cucumber, mint and labneh.

add-146.title: Chicken Maqalqal
add-146.culturalNotes: Maqalqal is a quick Gulf and Yemeni dish in which the meat is cut very small and stirred over high heat until the sauce dries and clings to the pieces.

instructions.1: Heat the oil on high heat, add the chicken and stir quickly until it changes colour all over.
instructions.2: Add the onion, garlic and pepper and stir until the onion softens.
instructions.3: Add the tomato, tomato paste, spices and salt and stir over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until the sauce almost dries.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with coriander and serve hot with bread or rice.

add-147.title: Lamb Maqalqal
add-147.culturalNotes: Cutting the meat into very small pieces lets it cook quickly and stay tender in this Gulf dish.

add-147-i1.name: Lamb or beef, very small cubes

add-147-i7.name: Cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, ground cardamom and black pepper

instructions.1: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot on high heat and brown the meat in batches.
instructions.2: Return all the meat, add the onion, garlic, peppers and spices and stir 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the tomatoes and salt, cover and cook on low heat 15-20 minutes until the meat is tender in its own juices, adding a little water if needed.
instructions.4: Uncover and stir on high heat until the sauce dries and caramelises onto the meat.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with coriander and serve with bread and sahawiq.

add-148.title: Homemade Saj Bread
add-148.culturalNotes: The thinner the loaf and the hotter the saj, the softer and lighter the bread. Freeze extra loaves and warm for a few seconds.

instructions.1: Knead the ingredients with the warm water added gradually into a soft, supple dough; cover 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Divide into medium balls, roll each very thin with a rolling pin, then stretch over the backs of your hands until translucent.
instructions.3: Heat a saj or the back of a large upturned pan on high heat and drape the bread over it.
instructions.4: Flip after 30-40 seconds when bubbles and brown spots appear, and leave a few seconds on the other side.
instructions.5: Fold the loaves and cover with a cloth; use for shawarma, sandwiches and manakish.

add-149.title: Yemeni Lahsa with Cheese
add-149.culturalNotes: Lahsa is a quick Yemeni breakfast, named because it is scooped up ('licked') with bread. The melted cheese makes it creamy.

instructions.1: Sauté the onion and chilli in the ghee until soft, then add the tomatoes and stir until they soften and cook down.
instructions.2: Crack the eggs over the mixture and stir quickly with the spices until they start to set.
instructions.3: Add the cheese and stir until it melts into the eggs and the texture is soft and creamy.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with coriander and serve hot with malawah or baladi bread.

add-150.title: Sheikh al-Mahshi (Stuffed Zucchini in Yogurt)
add-150.culturalNotes: It is called 'sheikh of the stuffed vegetables' because it is filled only with meat and no rice. Stirring the yogurt constantly until it boils stops it splitting.

add-150-i10.name: Crushed garlic and dried mint fried in ghee

instructions.1: Core the zucchini with a corer, wash and dry, and fry them in oil until lightly coloured if you like, then drain.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion, add the meat and spices and cook through, then add the pine nuts.
instructions.3: Stuff the zucchini with the meat and arrange in a pot.
instructions.4: Add a little water to cover and cook 15 minutes until tender.
instructions.5: Whisk the yogurt with the egg, starch and salt and cook over medium heat stirring in one direction until it boils, then pour over the zucchini and simmer 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Fry the garlic and dried mint in ghee and pour over the top; serve with vermicelli rice.

add-151.title: Yemeni Malawah (Flaky Salted Bread)
add-151.culturalNotes: Malawah is a flaky Yemeni bread traditionally baked in a tannour; its many layers resemble Egyptian feteer. It is served with saltah, honey and fenugreek.

instructions.1: Knead the flour and salt with the water added gradually into a very soft, smooth dough; divide into balls, brush with butter and cover 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Stretch each ball on a greased surface until paper-thin, brush with butter and sprinkle with nigella seeds.
instructions.3: Roll the sheet into a rope, then coil it like a snail and rest 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Press the coil with your palms into a disc 1 cm thick.
instructions.5: Bake in a hot oven at 220°C for 15-20 minutes until golden, or cook on a greased griddle over medium heat, flipping.
instructions.6: Clap between your palms after baking to separate the layers, and serve with honey or saltah.

add-152.title: Peach Jam
add-152.culturalNotes: Peaches have less pectin than apricots, so they need lemon and a little longer to set.

instructions.1: Peel the peaches by dipping them a few seconds in boiling water then cold water, stone them and cut into cubes.
instructions.2: Mix the peaches with the sugar and leave an hour to release their juice.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil over medium heat, skimming, then simmer on low heat, stirring, for 30-40 minutes until thick.
instructions.4: Add the lemon five minutes before removing from the heat and test on a cold plate.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-153.title: Apple Cinnamon Jam
add-153.culturalNotes: Apples are very rich in pectin so the jam sets easily. Green apples give a tarter taste and paler colour.

add-153-i1.name: Apples, peeled, grated or small cubes

instructions.1: Peel the apples and grate coarsely or cut into small cubes, sprinkling with lemon juice so they don't brown.
instructions.2: Put the apples with the sugar, water and cinnamon in a pot over medium heat until boiling.
instructions.3: Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring, until the apples are translucent golden and the jam thickens.
instructions.4: Remove the cinnamon and pour hot into sterilised jars.

add-154.title: Mixed Berry Jam
add-154.culturalNotes: You can press half the batch through a fine sieve to remove seeds for a smoother jam. Frozen berries give excellent results and are available year-round.

add-154-i1.name: Mixed berries (raspberry, blueberry, blackberry), fresh or frozen

instructions.1: Wash and drain the berries and lightly crush half of them with a fork.
instructions.2: Cook the berries and sugar in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and it boils.
instructions.3: Boil 20-25 minutes, skimming and stirring, until thick, adding the lemon in the last 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Test on a cold plate and pour hot into sterilised jars.

add-155.title: Damask Rose Petal Jam
add-155.culturalNotes: Rose jam is a preserve of Damascene homes. Use fragrant, unsprayed roses; the citric acid is what restores their pink colour.

add-155-i4.name: Citric acid or juice of 1 lemon

instructions.1: Separate the petals and trim off their bitter white base, rinse gently and drain.
instructions.2: Rub the petals with ½ cup of the sugar until they wilt and release their colour; cover and leave overnight.
instructions.3: Boil the remaining sugar with the water until dissolved, add the petals and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the citric acid, which turns the colour bright pink, and cook 5 more minutes until thick.
instructions.5: Pour into small sterilised jars and serve with cheese and Middle Eastern sweets.

add-156.title: Msabbaha (Warm Chickpeas in Tahini)
add-156.culturalNotes: Msabbaha is hummus with tahini made with whole chickpeas instead of puréed ones, served warm at Levantine and Palestinian breakfasts.

add-156-i8.name: Olive oil, parsley and paprika to serve

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight with the bicarbonate, then rinse.
instructions.2: Boil in fresh water until very tender (about an hour), keeping a cup of the cooking water.
instructions.3: Whisk the tahini with the lemon, garlic, cumin, salt and a little cooking water into a creamy sauce.
instructions.4: Lightly crush a quarter of the chickpeas and mix all the hot chickpeas with the sauce.
instructions.5: Spoon into a dish and top with the chilli-lemon dressing, olive oil, parsley and paprika; serve warm.

add-157.title: Orange Marmalade
add-157.culturalNotes: The peel must be fully tender before the sugar goes in, as it won't soften afterwards. Orange seeds are a natural pectin source that helps it set.

instructions.1: Wash the oranges well, halve and squeeze, keeping the juice and the seeds (tie the seeds in a cloth; they are rich in pectin).
instructions.2: Cut the peel into very thin strips and soak with the juice, water and seed bag overnight.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil, then simmer 40 minutes until the peel is completely tender.
instructions.4: Remove the seed bag, add the sugar and lemon juice and boil hard 15-20 minutes, stirring, until it reaches setting point on a cold plate.
instructions.5: Leave 10 minutes so the peel spreads evenly, then pour into sterilised jars.

add-158.title: Fig Jam
add-158.culturalNotes: Fig jam with sesame and anise is a traditional Levantine preserve, served at breakfast with white cheese.

instructions.1: Wash the figs and remove the stems; quarter them or leave whole if small.
instructions.2: Mix with the sugar and leave 2 hours to release their juice.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil over medium heat, then simmer on low heat 35-40 minutes, stirring, until thick and darker.
instructions.4: Add the lemon and anise or mastic five minutes before removing, then the sesame or walnuts.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars.

add-159.title: Burger Sauce
add-159.culturalNotes: Chopped pickles and pickle juice are the secret of the sweet-tangy taste that resembles famous burger chains' sauce.

add-159-i8.name: Sugar and a pinch of black pepper

instructions.1: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl until smooth.
instructions.2: Cover and chill at least 30 minutes so the flavours blend; keeps 5 days in the fridge.

add-160.title: Beef Fajitas
add-160.culturalNotes: Slicing the beef against the grain and cooking it quickly over very high heat gives tender, not chewy, strips.

add-160-i1.name: Beef steak, thin slices against the grain

add-160-i6.name: Cumin, smoked paprika, oregano and chilli

add-160-i10.name: Tortillas, sour cream and salsa to serve

instructions.1: Marinate the beef with the oil, lemon, garlic, soy sauce and spices, cover and chill at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Heat an iron pan on very high heat and sear the beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned outside and still tender, then remove.
instructions.3: Stir-fry the vegetables in the same pan on high heat until slightly softened but still crisp.
instructions.4: Return the beef to the vegetables for a minute and serve at once with warm tortillas, sour cream and salsa.

add-161.title: Homemade Chili Flakes
add-161.culturalNotes: Wear gloves when handling hot chillies and avoid touching your eyes. Toasting the flakes a minute in a dry pan before use makes them more fragrant.

instructions.1: Wash and dry the chillies well and split them lengthwise (keep the seeds for more heat or remove them for less).
instructions.2: Arrange on a tray and dry in the oven at 60-70°C with the door slightly open for 3-4 hours until brittle, or in the sun for several days.
instructions.3: Let cool completely, then pulse briefly in a grinder for coarse flakes, or grind fine for chilli powder.
instructions.4: Store in an airtight jar away from light.

add-162.title: Braised Beef with Eggplant
add-162.culturalNotes: Frying or roasting the eggplant before adding it keeps its shape so it doesn't fall apart in the sauce, and deepens the flavour.

add-162-i8.name: Mixed spice, cinnamon and a pinch of black pepper

instructions.1: Sprinkle the eggplant with salt and leave 20 minutes, then dry and fry until golden, or brush with oil and roast in the oven.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, add the meat and stir until it changes colour, then the garlic and spices.
instructions.3: Add the tomato paste, tomatoes and water, cover and simmer an hour until the meat is tender.
instructions.4: Add the eggplant and pepper and cook 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
instructions.5: Serve with white rice.

add-163.title: Lime-Cured Black Olives
add-163.culturalNotes: Lime speeds up removing the bitterness of olives instead of soaking for weeks, but use only the clear water and rinse the olives well afterwards.

add-163-i3.name: Water
add-163-i3.standardAmount: 2 litres for the lime + for the brine

instructions.1: Wash and drain the olives; mix the lime with 2 litres of water and leave until it settles.
instructions.2: Pour only the clear water (not the sediment) over the olives and leave 24 hours, stirring every 5 hours.
instructions.3: Drain the olives and rinse several times, then soak in plain water changed twice a day for 3-4 days until the bitterness is gone.
instructions.4: Make a brine of water and salt (a cup of salt per 2 litres), pack the olives in jars with the chillies and lemon and cover with brine.
instructions.5: Top with a layer of olive oil, seal and leave a week before eating.

add-164.title: Kunafa Mabrouma (Rolled Kunafa Fingers)
add-164.culturalNotes: Mabrouma is a Levantine kunafa sweet traditionally filled with Aleppo pistachios. Tight rolling keeps the fingers from coming apart after baking.

add-164-i1.name: Fresh shredded kunafa dough at room temperature

instructions.1: Cut a long strip of kunafa about 20 cm and lay it flat.
instructions.2: Brush with melted ghee and lay a line of nuts along one end.
instructions.3: Roll the strip from that end into a tight finger and trim the excess.
instructions.4: Pack the fingers tightly in a ghee-greased tray and brush with the remaining ghee.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C with top and bottom heat for 25 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Pour the syrup over as soon as it comes out, then cut and garnish with pistachios.

add-165.title: Egyptian Linza (Coconut Cake with Custard)
add-165.culturalNotes: Linza is a popular Egyptian bakery sweet; the custard layer in the middle sets it apart from ordinary coconut cake.

instructions.1: Mix the milk, cornflour, cream powder and vanilla cold, then stir over heat until thick; cover until cool.
instructions.2: Cream the butter with the icing sugar, then add the eggs one at a time.
instructions.3: Add the flour, coconut, baking powder and salt alternately with the milk until smooth.
instructions.4: Spread two-thirds of the batter in a greased tray, then the cold custard, then spoon the rest of the batter on top.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes until the top colours.
instructions.6: Let cool completely, brush the top with jam if you like and cut into squares.

add-166.title: Soft 'Soufflé' Dough for Savory Pastries
add-166.culturalNotes: The dough is called 'soufflé' for its cotton-like lightness. The egg white and milk keep it soft until the next day.

add-166-i8.name: Egg yolk with a little milk for brushing

add-166-i9.name: Fillings as you like (cheese, chicken, sausage)

instructions.1: Mix the yeast and sugar with the warm milk, then add the oil and egg white.
instructions.2: Add the flour and salt gradually and knead until very soft and smooth and not sticky; cover an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into small balls, roll out, fill with your favourite filling and shape into fingers, triangles or rounds.
instructions.4: Leave 20 minutes to rise again and brush with the yolk and milk.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until golden.

add-167.title: Levantine Ouzi (Spiced Rice and Lamb Parcels)
add-167.culturalNotes: Ouzi is originally a whole lamb stuffed with rice; the filo parcels are a home way of serving it as elegant individual portions.

instructions.1: Brown the meat in 2 tbsp ghee, cover with hot water, add the bay leaves, spices and salt and cook an hour until tender, keeping the stock.
instructions.2: Stir the rice in a spoon of ghee, add stock to just cover it and the salt and cook until absorbed, then add the peas.
instructions.3: Mix the rice with the meat and half the nuts.
instructions.4: Brush two filo sheets with ghee and stack them in a small bowl; add a few nuts, then rice, gather the edges into a parcel and turn it out onto a tray.
instructions.5: Brush the parcels with ghee and bake at 190°C for 15-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
instructions.6: Serve with yogurt or cucumber-yogurt salad.

add-168.title: Orange Semolina Basbousa
add-168.culturalNotes: Zest in the batter and juice in the syrup give a clear, fresh orange flavour that lightens the sweetness of the basbousa.

add-168-i11.name: Syrup: sugar, water and orange juice
add-168-i11.standardAmount: 1½ cups sugar + 1 cup water + ½ cup juice

instructions.1: Boil the sugar and water, add the orange juice and simmer 5 minutes; let the syrup cool.
instructions.2: Mix the semolina, flour, coconut and baking powder.
instructions.3: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and zest, then add the orange juice, yogurt and oil.
instructions.4: Add the wet mix to the dry and stir in one direction until smooth, then pour into a greased tin.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C with bottom heat until the edges brown, then top heat until coloured.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over while hot.

add-169.title: Dry Tahini Powder and Instant Tahini Sauce
add-169.culturalNotes: A dry powder that keeps for months and turns into tahini sauce in a minute; handy for trips and small kitchens.

add-169-i7.name: For the sauce: lemon juice and vinegar

instructions.1: Toast the flour in a dry pan on low heat, stirring, until light beige, and toast the sesame separately until golden.
instructions.2: Grind the sesame fine, mix with the toasted flour and salt, sift and store in an airtight jar.
instructions.3: For the sauce: mix 2 tbsp of the powder with the oil, then the water, lemon, vinegar and cumin, and whisk until creamy.
instructions.4: Serve the sauce at once with falafel, shawarma and grills.

add-170.title: Oven Tandoori Chicken
add-170.culturalNotes: Kashmiri chilli gives the signature red colour without fierce heat. Marinating in two stages, lemon first then yogurt, makes the chicken very tender.

instructions.1: Score the thighs deeply and marinate with the lemon, half the garlic and ginger, half the chilli and the salt for 20 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the yogurt with the remaining garlic, ginger and chilli, the masala, pepper and mustard, coat the chicken well and chill 4 hours or overnight.
instructions.3: Place the chicken on a rack over a tray and bake at 220°C for 35 minutes, turning once.
instructions.4: Baste with butter and grill 5 minutes until the edges char slightly.
instructions.5: Serve with sliced onion, lemon and mint yogurt sauce.

add-171.title: Pressure-Cooker Lamb Mandi
add-171.culturalNotes: A pressure cooker cuts the cooking of lamb to under an hour, and smoking with an ember at the end gives the tannour flavour without an oven.

add-171-i7.name: Cinnamon stick, coriander seeds, cardamom, bay leaves and peppercorns
add-171-i7.standardAmount: 1 stick + ½ tsp + 7 pods + 2 leaves + ½ tsp

instructions.1: Season the meat with the salt, pepper, turmeric and half the saffron.
instructions.2: Put the meat in the pressure cooker with the whole spices and water to cover and cook 35-40 minutes until tender, then lift out and strain the stock.
instructions.3: Brown the meat under the oven grill or in a pan until coloured.
instructions.4: Stir the rice in the oil for 2 minutes, add the stock (1½ times the rice volume) and salt, cook until absorbed, then cover on low heat for 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the remaining saffron, lay the meat on the rice, smoke with the ember inside the closed pot for 10 minutes and garnish with raisins.

add-172.title: Roast Duck à l'Orange
add-172.culturalNotes: Pricking the duck skin lets the thick layer of fat melt and drain, so the skin crisps and the meat isn't greasy.

add-172-i7.name: Cinnamon sticks, bay leaves and cardamom

instructions.1: Dry the duck well and prick the skin with a fork without reaching the meat; season inside and out with salt, pepper and orange zest.
instructions.2: Stuff with the onion, half an orange and the whole spices.
instructions.3: Place on a rack over a tray with a cup of water, cover and roast at 180°C for 1½ hours, pouring off the fat that collects.
instructions.4: Mix the orange juice, honey, soy sauce and butter.
instructions.5: Uncover and baste the duck with the mixture every 10 minutes for 30-40 minutes until the skin is glossy brown and crisp.
instructions.6: Boil the remaining mixture with the pan juices and cornflour until thick, rest the duck 15 minutes before carving and serve with the sauce.

add-173.title: Hummus el-Sham (Hot Spiced Chickpea Drink)
add-173.culturalNotes: Hummus el-Sham is an Egyptian winter drink sold from street carts, drunk very hot with chilli and lemon.

add-173-i5.name: Onion powder, garlic powder and cumin

add-173-i8.name: Chilli dressing: chickpea water and chilli

add-173-i9.name: Cumin dressing: chickpea water, cumin and lemon

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas 10-12 hours, then rinse.
instructions.2: Boil in plenty of water until fully cooked (about an hour).
instructions.3: Add the tomato juice, garlic, spices, stock cube and salt to the chickpeas with their water and boil 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Prepare the chilli and cumin-lemon dressings, each in a small bowl with chickpea water.
instructions.5: Serve the chickpeas with their broth piping hot in cups, adding a spoon of your favourite dressing to each.

add-174.title: Baked New York Cheesecake
add-174.culturalNotes: Low-speed mixing, a water bath and gradual cooling prevent cracks and give the famous dense, smooth texture.

add-174-i11.name: Strawberry or berry sauce to serve

instructions.1: Mix the biscuits and butter, press into a lined springform tin and bake 10 minutes at 170°C.
instructions.2: Beat the cream cheese with the sugar on low speed until smooth, then add the starch, sour cream, cream, lemon and vanilla.
instructions.3: Add the eggs one at a time, mixing lightly just until incorporated, without adding air.
instructions.4: Wrap the outside of the tin in foil, pour in the filling, set in a tray of hot water and bake at 160°C for 60-70 minutes until the edges set and the centre still wobbles slightly.
instructions.5: Turn off the oven and leave the cheesecake inside for an hour with the door ajar, then chill overnight.
instructions.6: Release the tin and serve with strawberry or berry sauce.

add-175.title: Damascene Madlouka with Ashta and Pistachio
add-175.culturalNotes: Madlouka is a Damascene sweet known for the green layer of pistachio covering the ashta. Toasting the semolina well in ghee is the secret of its flavour.

instructions.1: Toast the semolina in the ghee on low heat, stirring, until pale golden and fragrant.
instructions.2: Add the hot milk with the sugar, orange-blossom and rose water gradually, stirring constantly, until the semolina absorbs the liquid and becomes a smooth dough that leaves the pan.
instructions.3: Spread the hot dough in a serving dish 1-2 cm thick and smooth with a ghee-greased spoon.
instructions.4: Spread the ashta over it while warm or once cooled, and cover the whole top with crushed pistachios.
instructions.5: Cut into squares and serve with syrup on the side.
